jobs.description:
About Us

At BCD Meetings & Events (BCD M&E), we provide more than meeting and event planning services: we create connections that inspire, motivate and change behavior for our customers. As the world’s most trusted and innovative meetings and events agency, BCD M&E cultivates a culture of people, passion and purpose to drive business forward.

Headquartered in Chicago, with locations in 60+ countries across the world, BCD M&E’s team of 2,000+ people are committed to sustainability and driving success for our customers, our business and ourselves. Our values are at the heart of everything we do, and we look for people that want to be a part of something special, can rise to our standards and love to bring their unique perspective to the table.

While we can’t guarantee every day will be the best (who can?), we can promise a community of people who genuinely care and lead with empathy, a flexible workplace with awesome perks and challenging work that means something.

See what life is about at BCD M&E at bcdme.com/careers

About The Role

Love bringing complex events to life? As a Program Manager, you’ll lead the planning and execution of life science meetings and events, from congress-based programs to standalone meetings involving Healthcare Professionals, patients, colleagues, and speaker travel. You’ll be the go-to partner for clients, suppliers, and internal teams—keeping budgets, logistics, compliance, attendee details, and timelines running smoothly. If you thrive in a fast-moving environment and enjoy juggling multiple programs at once, this role will keep you energized.

You’re Good At

Managing life science meetings from kickoff to reconciliation, including budgets, attendee coordination, logistics, food and beverage, room setups, and technology needs
Building strong relationships with clients, suppliers, and internal teams while keeping communication clear, proactive, and professional
Navigating compliance requirements, maintaining audit-ready documentation, and following corporate guidelines and procedures
Using Cvent and Microsoft Office to manage attendee data, reporting, registration communications, and shared project materials accurately
Negotiating supplier contracts, coordinating vendors, and solving issues quickly to keep programs on track

You Might Also Have

At least 5 years of life science meetings management experience, especially with HCP programs
Experience supporting meetings connected to a Congress/Convention as well as standalone programs
A strong background in vendor management, sourcing, and contract negotiation
Previous experience with participant attendee management, travel planning, or destination knowledge
A college degree and Cvent Event Certification
Ability to work virtually

You Should Know

This role is virtual, operating on Eastern Standard Time
This role requires up to 25% annually
This role requires previous hands-on, full cycle, event management in the life sciences / pharmaceutical meetings & events space

THE PERKS

Flexible Working

We believe that a flexible working environment is key to getting the best out of our teams. We will support you to work where you need to and when you need to, depending on how you work best.

Room to Grow

Our line of work and business structure challenge our people in a way that inspires growth, with learning and development built into every role. We give individuals ownership over the direction and speed in which they grow.

Everyone has a voice

We thrive on conversations that spark curiosity and empathy. No matter how big or how small, every voice is heard, considered and respected.

Make your move

The diversity of roles across BCD M&E’s global locations means that our people often find new adventures during their time with us. Join us as a meeting planner role in the UK, stay for a global marketing career — there’s always room to move.

We’ve got you covered

Our extensive benefits include comprehensive healthcare, retirement plans, continued education support, diverse work locations, travel and hotel discounts, volunteer and sustainability opportunities and a successful employee recognition program.

We’re positive. You’ll love it.

It starts from the top. Our leaders lead with positivity, believe in our people and trust us to do the right thing. There will always be support along your journey, in little and big ways.

jobs.description:
THE POSITION

Do you prioritize being proactive and enjoy work that helps students with disabilities transition from school to employment? Apply for this Social Worker 2 position and serve as an Early Reach Coordinator for the Office of Vocational Rehabilitation (OVR), Bureau of Vocational Rehabilitation Services (BVRS), Pittsburgh District Office. This position supports Early Reach activities in Allegheny County by collaborating with local schools and education agencies to identify eligible students, begin services, and build connections that will lead to successful outcomes. You will also have the chance to promote public awareness of OVR services as well as work closely with families and schools. Apply now and start a role that helps students take important steps toward employment and independence.

DESCRIPTION OF WORK

This position creates key connections between students with disabilities, their families, schools, the community, and OVR resources to support students as they move from school to services and future employment. Your efforts will link students with resources, encourage positive attitudes toward work, and strengthen relationships with families and agencies. As a Social Worker 2, you will perform the following duties:

Liaise with Schools: Connect with the staff of local public and private schools and education agencies to answer their questions, provide disability and vocational consultation and training, and collaboratively create service provision plans and strategies
Encourage Students: Help students with disabilities develop positive attitudes toward work by using interest inventories and other tools to identify their aptitudes and abilities as well as how they can use this information to make and achieve employment goals
Provide Advocacy: Locate available community and educational services and resources, inform students and families of their rights, make initial and follow-up contacts as necessary to ensure appropriate services are provided
Promote Public Awareness: Provide trainings and presentations, attend conferences and meetings, and participate in other events to interact with and support students with disabilities and their families
Support Individualized Services: Gather and keep confidentiality for key personal and medical details from students and their families to help determine eligibility and inform the creation of individualized educational and service plans
Prepare Documentation: Complete application packets, case notes, and reports to help VR Counselors take over and open cases in a timely manner and to ensure accountability and accuracy in all activities

Project Access provides programs and services to over 27,000 children, families, and seniors living in affordable housing communities across the country. We strive to empower residents of affordable housing communities through our onsite services, aiming to create pathways for self-reliance and personal growth.

Join the Project Access team and create impact in the lives of our residents. Hear from them and how their lives have changed: www.project-access.org/success-stories/

The opportunity

The Resident Services Coordinator designs and implements programs that enhance community life for residents of all ages. They serve as a vital link between residents and services, creating value through targeted initiatives that address community needs. This role requires an innovative, proactive individual who excels in an autonomous environment, driving positive long-term outcomes through an understanding of the communities in which they serve.

The seniors residing at Silvey Villas live independently. The goal of this way of life is to maximize a resident’s dignity, autonomy, privacy, independence, choice, and safety. Residents are assisted in obtaining the services they need to maintain independence and the highest possible quality of life. We strive to keep residents as active and involved as possible through educational, social and recreational programs. The seniors are responsible for their own housing, meals, housekeeping, laundry, and personal care.

What You'll Do

Implement core programs and services, which include connecting, engaging, and empowering residents across four initiatives: Economic Stability, Education for Youth & Families, Health & Wellness, and Community Building.
Conduct outreach and survey resident needs through community engagement aligned with our four pillars.
Coordinate and oversee an after-school program and teen program encompassing homework assistance and educational enrichment activities.
Coordinate and oversee diversified programs, activities and special events for seniors, including bingo, arts and crafts, monthly birthday parties, and lite exercise programs, as space permits.
Independently plan, prepare, and facilitate resident-facing workshops and group sessions. When external partners are unavailable, deliver core topics directly to maintain consistency and resident engagement.
Develop & maintain partnerships with local providers to deliver services and workshops.
Plan & facilitate community-building events that foster safe and meaningful relationships between community members.
Provide residents with information & referrals to access community resources and services, specifically connecting residents with nonprofit partners who deliver services within our four pillars framework.
Support food distribution needs in the community, including maintaining food bank partnerships and distribution management.
Develop and maintain strong relationships with the property management team, scheduling regular communication sessions.
Organize and conduct monthly outreach requirements including door-to-door outreach, digital/virtual outreach, and physical presence in high-traffic locations.
Recruit, select, train, and oversee volunteers and interns who support programming at the Resource Center.
Use personal automobile to acquire program supplies and donations and attend offsite meetings (mileage reimbursed at IRS rate).

Collect & submit program outcomes data with emphasis on social impact data collection to measure outcomes within our four pillars.
Provide input and adhere to budgets for resident service programs, including authority to utilize funds for contractors when needed.

Experience in:

serving diverse populations, demonstrating cultural competency and community awareness.

Do you prioritize being proactive and enjoy work that helps students with disabilities transition from school to employment? Apply for this Social Worker 2 position and serve as an Early Reach Coordinator for the Office of Vocational Rehabilitation (OVR), Bureau of Vocational Rehabilitation Services (BVRS), Pittsburgh District Office. This position supports Early Reach activities in Allegheny County by collaborating with local schools and education agencies to identify eligible students, begin services, and build connections that will lead to successful outcomes. You will also have the chance to promote public awareness of OVR services as well as work closely with families and schools. Apply now and start a role that helps students take important steps toward employment and independence.

DESCRIPTION OF WORK

This position creates key connections between students with disabilities, their families, schools, the community, and OVR resources to support students as they move from school to services and future employment. Your efforts will link students with resources, encourage positive attitudes toward work, and strengthen relationships with families and agencies. As a Social Worker 2, you will perform the following duties:

Liaise with Schools: Connect with the staff of local public and private schools and education agencies to answer their questions, provide disability and vocational consultation and training, and collaboratively create service provision plans and strategies
Encourage Students: Help students with disabilities develop positive attitudes toward work by using interest inventories and other tools to identify their aptitudes and abilities as well as how they can use this information to make and achieve employment goals
Provide Advocacy: Locate available community and educational services and resources, inform students and families of their rights, make initial and follow-up contacts as necessary to ensure appropriate services are provided
Promote Public Awareness: Provide trainings and presentations, attend conferences and meetings, and participate in other events to interact with and support students with disabilities and their families
Support Individualized Services: Gather and keep confidentiality for key personal and medical details from students and their families to help determine eligibility and inform the creation of individualized educational and service plans
Prepare Documentation: Complete application packets, case notes, and reports to help VR Counselors take over and open cases in a timely manner and to ensure accountability and accuracy in all activities
